bull.b: Meaningfully positive operating and free cash flow gives Inspired greater capacity to fund content, platforms and customer deployments internally. If sustained, stronger conversion can support debt reduction and improve resilience despite the company’s leveraged capital structure.

The shift toward digital offerings and restructuring of lower-margin businesses has materially improved EBITDA margins. A better mix can support more durable earnings quality by allowing incremental revenue and operator usage to generate greater contribution over time.

Growth across Interactive and Virtual Sports, combined with debt retirement, indicates operating progress is being translated into balance-sheet improvement. Continued adoption of content and platforms could expand cash generation while reducing leverage and financial constraints.

bear.b: High debt relative to the business and persistent negative equity reduce financial flexibility and increase refinancing risk. These conditions can constrain investment, amplify the impact of weaker trading, and leave less capacity to absorb regulatory or operating setbacks.

Falling trailing revenue alongside continuing net losses weakens confidence in the durability of earnings, even with strong gross and operating margins. Sustained softness would make deleveraging more dependent on cost control and could limit internally funded growth.

Higher U.K. duties directly increase tax expense on gaming revenue and can compress Interactive and retail economics. Potential additional changes create lasting planning uncertainty, requiring Inspired to offset the burden through pricing, mix, efficiency or market expansion.
